guards.issue: MECHANISM EV-3, one verdict at every site (rule 3) -- see the CalculateVars EV-3 guard above for the mechanism statement and its executed evidence (`py audit/tools/event_probes.py eventrng`). RE-VERDICTED IN THE REVIEW FIX PASS, from waiver to gap. The prior rationale stated outright that this line "IS a real stream draw the sim does not take" and then filed it as a presentation waiver. That breaks two binding rules at once: rule 1, because a real unported draw is a gap (dormant at worst) and the waiver vocabulary is reserved for the four out-of-scope categories -- multiplayer, presentation, ascension, potions -- and this draw is none of them; and rule 3, because the identical mechanism (a `base.Rng` draw the sim never takes) is verdicted `gap` at 28 other entries across 27 records in this tier (counted programmatically over the event records), including the CalculateVars EV-3 guard in THIS record two entries up. Re-verified at source: JungleMazeAdventure.cs:60 is `List<(string, string)> shuffledFx = _fx.ToList().StableShuffle(base.Rng);`, the FIRST and unconditional statement of DontNeedHelp (the static `_fx` it shuffles is the 3-entry list at JungleMazeAdventure.cs:27-32), so a SOLO_QUEST resolution consumes the event stream even though nothing observable depends on the resulting order. It also carries EV-5's and EV-7's shape -- StableShuffle is sort-then-Fisher-Yates, so the draw count is fixed by the list length (3 entries) and the permutation by the sorted order -- which is a second reason a cosmetic shuffle cannot be waived: it is a deterministic, countable stream advance. The presentation half of this guard (waits, SFX) remains genuinely out of scope; it is recorded here rather than split out because a guard carries max(verdict) of what it aggregates. The unit rollup was already `gap` (EV-1 and the CalculateVars EV-3 guard), so this changes no rollup.
